name: Vegax Support – AI Customer Support & Order Status for WooCommerce
author: NCK Group LLC

sections.description:
Free plan: 100 conversations a month, no card required. Install, connect, and answer real customer questions before you decide anything about a paid plan.

Plans, and what each one covers:

  • Free – $0 – 100 conversations a month.
  • Starter – $79/month – 500 conversations a month.
  • Pro – $199/month – 2,500 conversations a month.
  • Enterprise – $399/month – 10,000 conversations a month.

Annual billing is available on the service site. These numbers are the same ones shown on the plugin directory listing and in the app listing, so you can compare without opening three tabs.

Vegax Support puts a support agent on your WooCommerce store. It reads your product catalogue and policy pages, so it answers from what you actually sell and how you actually do business — never on guesses.

  • Answers product, price, stock, shipping and returns questions.
  • Lets a customer check their own order status right in the chat (WISMO).
  • Replies in the language the customer writes in.
  • Chat bubble appears on your storefront without editing your theme.
  • Works with WooCommerce High-Performance Order Storage and the legacy post tables.

The Vegax service is required. The plugin itself is open-source (GPL) and is never locked or broken: you see the settings screen, the connect screen, the notices and the uninstall flow with or without a subscription. Only the answering engine lives outside your site.

A 7-day free trial is included. After the trial you can choose a plan to keep the service running. See vegaxclaw.com/woocommerce for current plans and pricing.

External services

This plugin relies on the Vegax service, a third-party hosted service, to generate support answers and order-status replies.

  • Service: Vegax — https://vegaxclaw.com
  • Base endpoint: https://office.vegaxclaw.com
  • Service terms of use: https://vegaxclaw.com/terms
  • Privacy policy: https://vegaxclaw.com/privacy

What the plugin sends and when

Each request identifies the store it belongs to — the two connection requests use the site URL instead, since the store is not connected yet. The catalogue, heartbeat and token-refresh payloads also carry the plugin version, and the catalogue, heartbeat and order-status payloads carry the time they were sent. None of those fields adds personal data.

The plugin contacts the Vegax service in two situations. (1) When an administrator starts the connection — pressing Connect with Vegax, or sending a one-time pairing code — the plugin asks the service for this store’s credentials. That call is made by the administrator, through an action protected by a capability check and a nonce, and it is what the connection itself needs. (2) Once the store is connected and the data-sharing consent checkbox on the settings screen is ticked, the plugin sends the data listed below. Connecting ticks that box for you; untick it, or press Disconnect, and no further data request leaves your site — the only remaining calls are those two connection requests, and they happen only when an administrator triggers them (Disconnect also deletes the stored credentials and removes every scheduled job).

  • Catalogue sync (separate from the heartbeat, triggered by an administrator or by the daily sync cron — never on heartbeat): product id, name, SKU, type, prices (regular, sale and current), on-sale flag, stock status, in-stock flag, stock quantity, categories, product link, image link, description (up to 600 characters: the short description, or the start of the full description when the short one is empty), attributes, weight, dimensions, variant data (options, price, sale price, stock) for up to 12 variations together with the total number of variations, plus the store key, the platform (woocommerce), the product count (with a note of how it was counted) and a site metadata block (site name, site URL, currency, locale, timezone, WooCommerce version, WordPress version, HPOS flag).
  • Policy pages and custom rules (shipping, returns, warranty and similar—named pages found on your own site), plus the FAQs and store rules the administrator types into the settings, as plain text: sent on the same sync.
  • Order status events (order number, status, status label, order date, total, currency, item count, shipped flag, shipment tracking numbers, providers and URLs, plus the ship date when the tracking entry carries one) and a hashed customer e-mail: sent when an order status changes. The clear-text e-mail is only sent if the administrator enables the “Send the customer e-mail with order events” option.
  • Daily heartbeat (a small status payload sent once a day): store key, site URL, site name, WordPress version, WooCommerce version, PHP version, currency, HPOS flag, order-lookup enabled flag, widget enabled flag, product count.
  • Token refresh (only for stores connected with the expiring-token connection, only when the access token is close to expiry, and only while the data-sharing consent checkbox is ticked): the store key, the refresh token and the plugin version, so the service can issue a fresh token pair. This runs in the background and is never triggered by a shopper’s page view.
  • Pairing request (only when the administrator uses the one-time pairing code or the Connect with Vegax authorization): the site URL, the one-time code and the plugin version; the Connect with Vegax authorization also sends the OAuth state value.
  • Identity token (only when the administrator switches on Identity verification, and only for a signed-in customer): a short-lived signed token carrying the customer id and the store key, and an expiry. It is a signature, not personal data — no name, e-mail or address is included.

The storefront chat widget script is loaded from the Vegax service so replies can be generated. It is only loaded when (a) the widget is enabled in the settings, (b) the store is connected to the service, and (c) the data-sharing consent checkbox is ticked. Turning consent off removes the script from the storefront on the next page view.

What is never sent

Customer names, addresses, phone numbers, order addresses and payment details are never transmitted. Your WordPress or WooCommerce credentials are never transmitted. No order data leaves your store in bulk: an order lookup answers either the single order a customer identified (when they supply the order number) or, when they only give the e-mail address they ordered with, at most the five most recent orders for that address.

Developers

The plugin exposes these filters, so a site can adapt the integration without editing the plugin:

  • vegax_ais_widget_tag_attributes — change the attributes printed on the chat widget tag.
  • vegax_ais_widget_should_render — decide whether the widget is printed on the current request.
  • vegax_ais_widget_on_checkout — print (or keep away from) the widget on the checkout page.
  • vegax_ais_knowledge_product — add, rename or drop fields for a product in the catalogue sync.
  • vegax_ais_heartbeat_payload — add or remove fields in the daily heartbeat.
  • vegax_ais_order_event_payload — add or remove fields in the order-status event.
  • vegax_ais_tracking_items — change the shipment tracking items read from an order.

Source code

The plugin is GPL-2.0-or-later, and its source is public at github.com/JulianClaw/vegax-support. Those are the same files released here, so the code on WordPress.org can be compared line by line. Bug reports and pull requests are welcome on the issue tracker; security reports should go to support@vegaxclaw.com rather than a public issue.
sections.installation:
1. Install WooCommerce and set up your products and policy pages.
  2. Install the “Vegax Support” plugin from the WordPress Plugin Directory.
  3. Go to WooCommerce > Vegax Support in your WordPress admin.
  4. Click Connect with Vegax on the settings screen and approve the store on the Vegax site — you are returned and the store connects automatically. (Stores that already hold a token and secret, or use a one-time pairing code, keep working exactly as before.)
  5. (Optional) Switch on Identity verification to tie chats to signed-in customers, then click Test connection to verify.
sections.faq:
Does this replace my staff?

It answers common questions and order-status lookups. It does not handle escalated support, exchanges, refunds or outbound calls — those still go to your team.

Can customers see my prices and stock?

Yes, through the widget. That is the point — so customers get immediate answers.

Is there a free plan?

Yes. The free plan covers 100 conversations a month with no card required: the widget answers from your catalogue and policy pages, and order-status lookups work the same way they do on a paid plan. If you outgrow it, you choose a plan; if you stop, the plugin keeps working as software and simply stops answering.

Where can I see the current plans and pricing?

At vegaxclaw.com/woocommerce.

Is the plugin open source?

Yes, it is GPL-2.0-or-later. The Vegax service is a paid subscription; the plugin itself is never locked or broken when the subscription expires. The source code, issue tracker and release history are public at github.com/JulianClaw/vegax-support — the same files that are released here.
sections.changelog:
1.0.15

  • The description now lists the plans with the same prices and conversation limits used in the app listing, so the two listings cannot drift apart.

1.0.14

  • Adds the screenshots section: the widget on a live storefront, a catalogue answer with variants and prices, an unpublished-policy answer, and the mobile view.

1.0.13

  • The free plan is stated in the short description and at the top of the description, where the plugin directory actually shows it.

1.0.12

  • The listing now states the free plan (100 conversations a month, no card) instead of leaving it to be discovered after install.
  • Plugin name includes what it does, so it is findable by search inside WordPress and on the plugin directory.
  • Tags updated to match how store owners search for support plugins.

1.0.11

  • Maintenance release. The public repository now carries a security policy (how to report a vulnerability privately, and what the plugin does and does not handle). No functional change to the plugin code.
  • Tested against WordPress 7.1.

1.0.10

  • The plugin source code, issue tracker and release history are public at https://github.com/JulianClaw/vegax-support (GPL-2.0-or-later, same files as released here), and the readme now says so.
  • The settings screen adds one line of text with two links: the public source code, and the WordPress.org review page. It is plain text inside the settings screen — no pop-up, no site-wide notice, no dismissal prompt and no incentive of any kind.

1.0.9

  • Security: the /health REST route is now restricted to WordPress administrators (manage_options). It reports plugin, WooCommerce, WordPress and PHP versions plus connection and synchronisation state, so it must not be readable by an anonymous visitor. Nothing in the Vegax service called that route, so no functionality changed.
  • The signature check for the /order-lookup and /knowledge routes now runs in each route’s permission_callback (the documented place for authorisation) instead of only inside the callback body, so every route declares its access rule explicitly.
  • The saved store token and secret are no longer printed back into the settings HTML. An empty field now means “keep the stored value”, and Disconnect is the way to erase credentials, so a shop manager can no longer read the signing secret in the page source.
  • A pairing link received by URL no longer changes settings by itself: the code is only staged until the administrator confirms it with the nonce-protected Connect button.
  • Disconnect now deletes the stored credentials including the expiring-token pair, clears the connection status shown on the settings screen and removes every scheduled job; uninstalling the plugin removes every scheduled job as well. The jobs are created again automatically once the store is connected again, so a reconnect never leaves the store without token renewal.
  • Data sharing is now enforced on both directions of every path: the catalogue sync, the heartbeat, the token refresh and the storefront widget script stop when the consent box is unticked, and the signed /order-lookup and /knowledge routes refuse to serve data while consent is withdrawn. Connecting the store ticks the consent box; it is unticked on a fresh install and can be unticked at any time.
  • The readme’s data lists were corrected to match the payloads the code actually sends.

1.0.8

  • One-click connect: the Connect with Vegax button sends the merchant to a Vegax authorization page that names the store, then returns and connects the store automatically using a single-use, short-lived code together with an anti-forgery state value. The older paste-a-pairing-code path is kept for backward compatibility and keeps working unchanged.
  • Added an optional Identity verification switch (off by default). When on, a signed-in customer is tagged with a short-lived signed token so a chat can never be answered for the wrong person (for example when a cache reuses a conversation).
  • Data sharing is now strictly opt-in: the consent checkbox is unticked by default on a fresh install, and the plugin sends nothing to the Vegax service until the administrator ticks it. (1.0.7 pre-ticked the box for the previous default.)
  • Unified the plugin name to a single identifier vegax-support everywhere: the plugin folder, the main file, the text domain, the readme and the data-plugin marker printed by the widget.
  • Changed the outbound User-Agent/plugin header value to Vegax-Support for consistency.
  • Updated the readme’s External services and Description sections so the documented fields match the payload that is actually sent.
  • The storefront widget tag is now guaranteed cache-safe: when Identity verification is on, a response that carries a signed customer token is marked uncacheable (DONOTCACHEPAGE plus no-cache headers plus Vary: Cookie), so a page cache or CDN can never hand one shopper’s verified chat to another visitor.
  • Consolidated all input sanitising and output escaping into one shared helper (Vegax_AIS_Safe) used by the admin screen and the storefront widget.
  • Added developer extension points — see the plugin README “Developers” section: vegax_ais_widget_tag_attributes, vegax_ais_knowledge_product, vegax_ais_heartbeat_payload, vegax_ais_order_event_payload.
  • Added a PHPUnit test suite and a GitHub Actions workflow (syntax check across PHP versions, PHPUnit, PHPCS) for maintainers.
  • The connection now uses a short-lived access token together with a longer-lived refresh token (issued when the store is connected). The plugin reads the lifetime from the service response and renews the pair in the background (a WordPress cron job) before it expires — never during a shopper’s page view, so the storefront is never slowed down. If a renewal cannot be completed the store pauses sending data instead of failing, and the settings screen shows a Reconnect with Vegax prompt. Stores connected with the older static token and secret keep working exactly as before.

1.0.7

  • Complete rewrite of the WordPress.org listing readme: every data field now matches the actual payload and each outbound call is documented separately (catalogue sync, heartbeat, order event, pairing request).
  • Added explicit data-sharing consent checkbox (WooCommerce > Vegax Support). The checkbox is pre-ticked for stores that were already connected; on a fresh install it is unticked until the store connects.
  • Added in-plugin disconnect action that clears all credentials and stops all outbound traffic.
  • Added in-plugin privacy policy text (Tools > Privacy).
  • Widget script no longer loads before the store is connected — prevents any pre-consent phone-home.
  • Brand text is “Vegax Support” with no engine name shown to shoppers.
  • Plugin header requires at least WordPress 6.5 (for Requires Plugins support).
  • Removed stale Domain Path: /languages header (directory did not exist).

1.0.6

  • Removed the old default name from every user-facing screen. The canned agent name “Vegax Support” replaces the previous default.
  • Brand colour defaults to #07A87F (#18B287 was the old one).
  • Added HPOS compatibility declaration.
  • Added custom store rules and merchant FAQ fields to the settings screen.
  • Widget is hidden on the checkout page by default.

1.0.0

  • Initial release.

upgrade_notice.1.0.9: Security release. The status route is now administrator-only, every route declares its own access rule, saved credentials are no longer printed back into the settings page, Disconnect removes every credential, saved status and scheduled job, and data sharing is enforced on requests in both directions. Please update.
upgrade_notice.1.0.8: Data sharing is now opt-in. After updating, the plugin stops sending your catalogue and order status events until you tick "Data sharing" on the WooCommerce > Vegax Support settings screen. The storefront widget keeps working once the store is connected.
upgrade_notice.1.0.7: The widget script no longer loads before the store is connected. If you had the widget enabled but kept the token/secret fields empty, you will not see the widget until you connect.
